iWant: the package to carry only the tool, not rcf-lite's own requirements chain
soThat: reviewer names, verdicts and the rulings ledger of the tool's own development never land in my node_modules
description: Privacy: rcf/ leaves the npm files (contract C1, ruling R3).
title: An adopter installs rcf-lite from npm and receives none of rcf-lite's own chain

acceptanceCriteria.description: [must-not] Given packages/rcf-lite at the reviewed head, when `npm pack --dry-run --json` runs in packages/rcf-lite (the real npm pack, its prepack included), then it exits 0 and the file list it prints holds no file whose path starts with `rcf/`.

[happy] Given the tarball `npm pack` produces in packages/rcf-lite, installed with `npm install ` into a fresh empty directory, when the installed package's bin runs, in that directory, `rcf init`, `rcf doctor`, `rcf guidance build-cycle`, the MCP server (`rcf mcp`) answering `resources/list`, and `rcf audit view --port

` (then stopped with SIGTERM sent to its own pid), then each exits 0, the installed package holds no `rcf/` folder, and no command reads, stats or lists any path under the installed package's `rcf/`. External: the 0.41.0 release Verify also runs this journey.

[must-not] Given the tarball `npm pack` produces in packages/rcf-lite, when every packed file is read (including `guidance/`, `guidance/discovery/`, `src/`, `blueprints/`, `fixtures/`, `releases/` and `CHANGELOG.md`), then none carries rcf-lite development-chain material: no named reviewer, stage-keeper or operator; no relay, work-item, dispatch or lane job id (shapes `relay <uuid>`, `w-YYYY-MM-DD-...`, `d-YYYY-MM-DD-NNN`, `r-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxx`); no verdict record; no quoted or cited development ruling. In particular the tarball carries neither `Dave 2026-10-07` nor relay `9d3dd0a3-e7e5-4c6a-985e-c3962be38d4c`.

[must-not] Given the tarball `npm pack` produces in packages/rcf-lite, when every packed file is read (including `guidance/`, `src/`, `blueprints/`, `fixtures/`, `releases/` and `CHANGELOG.md`), then none carries a developer home directory (a path `/Users/<name>/...` or `/home/<name>/...`), an internal specification or estate path (a path `projects/<name>/specs/`, `spec/`, `docs/`, `wireframes/` or `notes/`, or a path into a maintainer's agent workspace, `agents/<name>/notes/` and kin), or the name of a consumer project, a consuming team or a developer handle. The consumer, team and handle names are a list the maintainers keep outside the public tree, read from the repository secret `RCF_PRIVACY_FORBIDDEN_TERMS` (one term per line, matched whole-word and without regard to case).

[must-not] Given the tarball `npm pack` produces in packages/rcf-lite, when the privacy scan of AC-20501-3 and AC-20501-4 reads every packed file, then a file it cannot read as plain text (bytes that do not decode as UTF-8, or a line holding a base64 or hex run of 64 or more characters) is named by its path as unscanned and the check fails; such a file passes only when its path is on the allow-list the maintainers record in the chain's decisions ledger.

[must-not] Given a run of the AC-20501-4 privacy check where the consumer, team and handle list is expected (the repository's own CI and its publish workflow, each declaring it with `RCF_PRIVACY_TERMS_EXPECTED` on the step that runs the suite), when `RCF_PRIVACY_FORBIDDEN_TERMS` is empty or missing, then the check fails, naming the missing list, and never passes; in a run where the list is not expected (a local run, or a fork's CI) and it is missing, the consumer class is reported as skipped, with one printed line naming it as skipped, and never as passed.
